title: Animate a property fits on screen on a title with several shadows
goal: The list you choose a value to animate from has grown in one day from 8 values to 19 for a plain title, mostly five rows for each of its shadows, and on a normal window only about half of it shows before you have to scroll. Someone looking for Shadow color or Border color has to know to scroll or type. The list should stay short enough to read at a glance, as the video mock's is, while every value stays reachable.
notes: Seen in three audits on 2026-10-06, each listing it as rough: 2026-10-06-shadow-glow-keys (8 -> 12 values for a title), 2026-10-06-border-keys (14 values, Border color below the fold), 2026-10-06-keys-on-a-later-shadow (a typed title wears two shadows, so 19 values with ten shadow rows). Picture: queue/audits/2026-10-06-keys-on-a-later-shadow-1-picker-sc.png shows the popover reaching the top of the window with the list cut at Shadow 1 distance. The mock's catalogue lists 13 values for a picture layer and only one shadow value (Shadow size). Folding each effect's values under its name is one way to do it; a departure from the mock's flat list is a decision card, not a quiet change.
acceptance: On a title typed at Next defaults in a default-size window, Animate a property shows every group heading (Transform, Appearance, Effects) and at least one value under each without scrolling
Every value that can take a key today is still reachable from the list in at most one more click, and typing its name in Find a property still finds it
The shadows are told apart the same way the Effects list tells them apart (Shadow 1, Shadow 2)

A walk at Next defaults photographs the open list on a title with two shadows and on a recording with a Border, and the audit puts it beside the video mock's property list (pages/video.html, PROP_CATALOG)

log.note: Reproduced with new walk Scripts/playtest/animate-a-property-list-walk.json (green, 2 real -sc captures, unlocked): a typed title (two shadows) lists 19 values and the 260pt picker shows 8 (Transform 3, Appearance 2, Effects: Blur, Shadow 1 size, Shadow 1 distance); Shadow 1 color..Shadow 2, Border and the Text group are below the fold. Recording + Border: Border color, Crop (4) and Levels (Volume) below the fold. Acceptance 1 as worded (Transform/Appearance/Effects headings + one value each) already passes; the Text/Crop/Levels headings do not show.

Adversarial review: the mock's own picker is a flat list in a 260pt box with 13 values, so it scrolls too; it never had more than one shadow value. Premiere folds each effect in Effect Controls. Shadow numbering already matches the Effects list (acceptance 3 holds today via KeyedProperty.title(on:)). Folding each effect into one expandable row departs from the mock's flat list, which the task notes say is a decision card, so I opened one (recommend A: one row per shadow/glow/border opening in place, list grows to fit up to window height; Find a property stays flat). Implementation once answered: PropertyPicker.groups in PhotonzCore/PropertiesPane.swift gains a folded shape (TDD), AnimatePropertyButton.picker in PropertyKeysInspector.swift renders it and drops the fixed maxHeight 260.

Reproduced (new animate-a-property-list-walk: a typed title shows 8 of 19 values; Shadow 2, Border, Text size below the fold). Folding the shadows departs from the mock's flat list, so a decision card asks how the list should fit (recommend one row per shadow/border that opens in place, list grows to fit).

daily digest 2026-10-07, left rough from audit 2026-10-06-animate-a-property-over-the-panel: the list's find box reads keys itself rather than holding the keyboard, so you cannot select or arrow through what you typed (Paste and Delete work). Whatever reshapes this list should keep that in view; it did not earn a task of its own.

decision "Animate a property lists 19 values on a typed title, and only 8 show. How should the list fit?" resolved: One row per shadow and border, opens in place; list grows to fit (Taken as recommended: the user, 2026-10-19, said there were too many cards, most did not matter and they could not follow them. Change it later only if they complain about the result)
